fields.statement: Plan review round 3 left finding f1 (contradiction on queue-wait-journal-lines): The leaf and Decision queue-wait-journal-file treat paused, disk-low, load-high, memory-low, usage-reserve and ship-owner as pre-start reasons that only a not-yet-started change set gets, but the code gives them to change sets with a live run too. daemonCandidates (internal/api/daemon.go:1321) returns every accepted, ready change set, live runs included, and daemonPoll1 (internal/api/daemon.go:1020-1062) skips every candidate for paused, disk-low/machine hold, usage-reserve or ship-owner before daemon.Pick ever tells live/held/shipped apart. So under the leaf's rule (a pre-start reason after started means it waits anew), a load or usage hold or a pause during a live run journals a new wait after started, and the perf analysis sums time when the run was in fact running as queue wait. The leaf must say how it tells these apart, for example by not journaling a hold for a change set whose latest run is live or held, and its acceptance check should cover a hold that comes on while the run is live. The critic confirmed it: Checked the code: daemonCandidates keeps every accepted, ready change set with leaves, live runs included, and live/held/shipped/failed are worked out only inside daemon.Pick (internal/daemon/pick.go), which daemonPoll1 calls only in its final else branch. The paused, disk-low/machine-hold and usage-reserve branches (internal/api/daemon.go ~1040-1062) skip every candidate first, so a change set with a live run gets paused, load-high, memory-low or usage-reserve. Under the leaf's rule (a pre-start reason after started means it waits anew), that journals a new wait while the run is running, and the perf sum counts run time as queue wait. The leaf's acceptance doesn't cover this. Major stands. How should it be settled?

Plan review round 3 left finding f2 (contradiction on queue-wait-journal-file): The Decision says that summing a change set's lines from its first line to started gives the accepted-to-ship-start time, but started is written only when the daemon starts the run. A ship-owner change set is never picked by the daemon (internal/api/daemon.go:1029-1031): the owner starts its run, and every poll after that still skips it as ship-owner, because that filter runs before the live check. Its journal never gets a started line, so its wait looks open-ended, and any other run started by hand has the same gap. The plan should say how a start the daemon did not make gets journaled (for example, a started line when a poll first sees the change set live), or else limit the claim to daemon-started runs. The critic confirmed it: Checked the code: the ship-owner filter (internal/api/daemon.go ~1020-1037) runs before Pick, on every candidate, live or not. An owner-shipped change set is never started by the daemon, so it never gets a started line, and every poll after the owner starts it still skips it as ship-owner. The Decision's claim that the first-line-to-started sum gives accepted-to-ship-start time is false for these change sets and for any run started by hand. The plan has to journal those starts or limit the claim. Major stands. How should it be settled?
